title: Bags and Coins
statementMd:
When you were a child you must have been told a puzzle of bags and coins. Anyway, here's one of its versions:

*A horse has three bags. The first bag has one coin, the second bag has one coin and the third bag has three coins. In total, the horse has three coins in the bags. How is that possible?*

The answer is quite simple. The third bag contains a coin and two other bags.

This problem is a generalization of the childhood puzzle. You have $*n*$ bags. You know that the first bag contains $*a*_{1}$ coins, the second bag contains $*a*_{2}$ coins, ..., the $*n*$-th bag contains $*a*_{*n*}$ coins. In total, there are $*s*$ coins. Find the way to arrange the bags and coins so that they match the described scenario or else state that it is impossible to do.

## Input

The first line contains two integers $*n*$ and $*s*$ $(1 ≤ *n*, *s* ≤ 70000)$ — the number of bags and the total number of coins. The next line contains $*n*$ integers $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$ $(1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 70000)$, where $*a*_{*i*}$ shows the number of coins in the $*i*$-th bag.

## Output

If the answer doesn't exist, print `-1`.

Otherwise, print $*n*$ lines, on the $*i*$-th line print the contents of the $*i*$-th bag. The first number in the line, $*c*_{*i*}$ $(0 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ *a*_{*i*})$, must represent the number of coins lying directly in the $*i*$-th bag (the coins in the bags that are in the $*i*$-th bag are not taken into consideration). The second number in the line, $*k*_{*i*}$ $(0 ≤ *k*_{*i*} < *n*)$ must represent the number of bags that lie directly in the $*i*$-th bag (the bags that are inside the bags lying in the $*i*$-th bag are not taken into consideration). Next, the line must contain $*k*_{*i*}$ integers — the numbers of the bags that are lying directly in the $*i*$-th bag.

The total number of coins in the solution must equal $*s*$. If we count the total number of coins the $*i*$-th bag in the solution has, we should get $*a*_{*i*}$.

No bag can directly lie in more than one bag. The bags can be nested in more than one level (see the second test case). If there are multiple correct answers, you can print any of them.

## Note

The pictures below show two possible ways to solve one test case from the statement. The left picture corresponds to the first test case, the right picture corresponds to the second one.

statementZhMd:
小时候，你一定听说过一个关于袋子和硬币的谜题。无论如何，下面是其中的一个版本：

*一匹马有三个袋子。第一个袋子里有一枚硬币，第二个袋子里有一枚硬币，第三个袋子里有三枚硬币。总共来说，马的袋子里有三枚硬币。这怎么可能呢？*

答案非常简单。第三个袋子里装着一枚硬币和另外两个袋子。

本题是这个童年谜题的推广。现在有 $*n*$ 个袋子。你知道第一个袋子包含 $*a*_{1}$ 枚硬币，第二个袋子包含 $*a*_{2}$ 枚硬币，……，第 $*n*$ 个袋子包含 $*a*_{*n*}$ 枚硬币。所有袋子中总共有 $*s*$ 枚硬币。请找出一种排列袋子和硬币的方式，使其符合上述描述；如果无法做到，则说明这一点。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*s*$（$1 ≤ *n*, *s* ≤ 70000$），分别表示袋子的数量和硬币总数。下一行包含 $*n*$ 个整数 $*a*_{1}, *a*_{2}, ..., *a*_{*n*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*i*} ≤ 70000$），其中 $*a*_{*i*}$ 表示第 $*i*$ 个袋子中的硬币数量。

## 输出格式

如果不存在答案，输出 `-1`。

否则，输出 $*n*$ 行，第 $*i*$ 行输出第 $*i*$ 个袋子的内容。该行的第一个数 $*c*_{*i*}$（$0 ≤ *c*_{*i*} ≤ *a*_{*i*}$）表示直接放在第 $*i*$ 个袋子中的硬币数量（不考虑位于第 $*i*$ 个袋子中的袋子里的硬币）。该行的第二个数 $*k*_{*i*}$（$0 ≤ *k*_{*i*} < *n*$）表示直接位于第 $*i*$ 个袋子中的袋子数量（不考虑位于第 $*i*$ 个袋子中的袋子里的袋子）。接下来，该行还应包含 $*k*_{*i*}$ 个整数，表示直接位于第 $*i*$ 个袋子中的袋子的编号。

解中硬币的总数必须等于 $*s*$。如果计算解中第 $*i*$ 个袋子所拥有的硬币总数，结果应为 $*a*_{*i*}$。

任何袋子都不能直接位于多个袋子中。袋子可以多层嵌套（参见第二个样例）。如果有多个正确答案，可以输出任意一个。
